sources.entry: cc-probeline by labzink - See where it leaks, stop paying for it — a live Claude Code status line that prices every turn, your subagents, cache rebuilds, plus limits, context and git.

summary.one_liner: A Claude Code status line that prices each turn, subagent work, and cache rebuild from the local session log, alongside limits, context, and git info.
summary.what_it_does: Reads the session JSONL log on disk and the status-line payload Claude Code sends, then renders a live status line. It shows a per-turn cost table where each turn and each subagent turn is priced as an estimate against a public price table. It tracks prompt-cache TTL countdowns (60 min for the orchestrator, 5 min for subagents) and prices cache rebuilds when they happen. It also shows 5h and 7d rate-limit usage with reset times, extra-usage spend in dollars, context-window fill, model, git, and session time, with colour zones for warning levels. A /cc-probeline-config wizard or a TOML file controls which segments show and their thresholds. The README says rendering is offline; the only network calls are optional, opt-out price/version checks and a background refresh of Claude Code's /usage cache.
use_cases: monitor Claude Code session cost per turn
see what subagents spend while they run
track 5h and 7d rate limits in the terminal
spot prompt cache rebuilds and their dollar cost
watch context window fill during a session
customise a Claude Code status line without hand-editing config
how_to_run: curl -fsSL | sh # macOS / Linux (the README's URL is empty in the source)
/plugin marketplace add labzink/cc-probeline # Claude Code plugin marketplace
cc-probeline --check # verify installation; prints Installation OK
/cc-probeline-config # interactive config wizard inside Claude Code
stack: Go (single compiled binary, no runtime dependencies)
Claude Code status line and plugin system
notable: Prices every turn, subagent turn, and cache rebuild live, labelled as estimates from a public price table
Optional daily price/version check over the network, falling back to the table baked into the build when offline or opted out
Shows extra-usage spend in dollars against a monthly ceiling, taken from Anthropic's own figure
Release artifacts ship with SHA256 checksums and signed SLSA build provenance
README states that the development was done through an AI-agent pipeline; code contributions are accepted only through that workflow
caveats: The quota segment (5h / 7d limits, extra usage) requires Claude Code 2.1.80 or newer; on older versions it is hidden
Per-turn costs are estimates computed from token counts against a public price table
Scoop install is marked experimental; uninstalling via Scoop requires running cc-probeline uninstall first
